mainTopic: Redeeming a consecrated inherited field (שדה אחוזה): counting years, the fixed price by area, and who keeps the field at the יובל
overview: This amud is about redeeming an inherited field that someone gave to הקדש. It opens by explaining that only full years lower the redemption price. A leftover part of a year is never subtracted. A ברייתא learns from the word 'years' in ויקרא 27:18 that months are not counted to lower the price, and it learns from 'וחשב לו הכהן' that הקדש may count months as a full year when that helps it. A new משנה sets the price at fifty שקלים for an area sown with a חומר of barley, divided by the years left until the יובל and paid all at once. Only the owner adds a חומש. The גמרא defines the measure as seed sown by hand at an average thickness. It explains that deep crevices are left out because they are full of water and cannot be sown, while shallow dips and low rocks count as part of the field. Another משנה then tells who keeps a redeemed field at the יובל: the owner or his son keeps it, but if someone else redeemed it first it goes to all the כהנים.

steps.title: After the Jubilee really means during the Jubilee cycle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'after the יובל' in the משנה means any time within the יובל cycle. As long as a year is not complete, it is not subtracted from the price.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means in the middle of the יובל cycle. As long as a year has not been completed, it is not deducted from the price.
steps.whatsHappening: Just before this, the גמרא asked how the משנה could speak about redeeming a field 'after the יובל'. Here we hear the end of the גמרא's own answer: it means during the cycle, and a partial year never lowers the price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The redemption price of a consecrated field goes down for each year that has passed toward the יובל. The גמרא says only full years count for that reduction. So with 5½ years left, you pay for 6 years, not 5½.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jubilee year (every 50th year), when fields return to their original owners
In the middle of the יובל cycle, meaning any time during the 50 years
Deducts, subtracts from the price

phrases.english: In the middle of the Jubilee cycle,

phrases.aramaic: דְּכֹל כַּמָּה דְּלָא מָלְיָא לֵיהּ שָׁנָה
phrases.english: for as long as a year has not been completed for him,
he does not deduct it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer to a question asked just before this section begins
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a phrase in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seems to speak about after the יובל has already passed, which makes no sense
steps.terutzMaskana: It means during the יובל cycle: partial years are not subtracted from the price
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only complete years reduce the redemption price of a consecrated field

steps.title: Why say it, if the next line of the משנה says it outright?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what this part of the משנה is adding. The rule that months are not counted against הקדש is stated directly in the very next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the משנה teaching us here? That we don't count months against הקדש? But it says that explicitly: 'We do not count months with הקדש'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own anonymous reading. If this line means 'partial years don't count', it seems to repeat the next line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is not supposed to repeat itself for no reason. Under the גמרא's anonymous reading, 'not less than a year' and 'we don't count months with הקדש' teach the same rule. So one of them seems extra.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? (asking what new point is being made)
The Temple treasury / consecrated property
Counting months (as part of the price calculation)
Explicitly, openly

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?
That one does not count months with the Temple treasury?
phrases.notes: He means you can't use leftover months to lower the price you owe הקדש.

phrases.english: But it is taught explicitly:
"One does not count months with the Temple treasury!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading given in step 1 because it seems to make the משנה repeat itself
steps.kashyaTarget: The גמרא's anonymous reading of 'not less than a year after the יובל'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that line means partial years don't count, it is the same as the next explicit line of the משנה, so one of them is extra

steps.title: The משנה is giving the reason for the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is written in a 'what is the reason' style. The second line explains the first: we can't redeem for less than a year's price because months are not counted against הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is saying 'what is the reason': why can't one redeem after the יובל for less than a year? Because we don't count months with הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The second line is not a new rule; it explains the reason for the first line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra wording is no longer extra. The first line gives the rule (partial years are paid as full years), and the second gives the reason (months are not counted against הקדש). Together they form one teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It is saying 'what is the reason', meaning the second part explains the first
Redeem (buy back the field from הקדש)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is not repeating itself. 'Not less than a year' is the rule, and 'we don't count months with הקדש' is its reason.

phrases.english: It is saying "what is the reason":
What is the reason that one does not redeem
after the Jubilee for less than a year?

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּאֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין חֳדָשִׁים עִם הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ.
phrases.english: Because one does not count months with the Temple treasury.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the משנה as rule plus reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two lines of the משנה seem to state the same rule twice
steps.terutzMaskana: The second line gives the reason for the first, so nothing is repeated

steps.title: Asking for the source that months are not counted against the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא. The ברייתא asks where we learn that months are not counted to lower the price owed to הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'We do not count months' and so on. The רבנן taught: From where do we know that we do not count months with הקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks for its source in the תורה. This sets up the פסוק that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the גמרא was explaining how the משנה is worded. Now it looks for the root of the rule itself. The question 'מנין' asks which פסוק teaches it.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc., meaning the quote of the משנה continues
From where? (asking for a source in the תורה)
A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה

phrases.english: "One does not count months," etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the next line of the משנה, which goes on: 'but הקדש does count months.'

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
From where do we know that one does not count months
with the Temple treasury?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין חֳדָשִׁים וְכוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה and asks for its source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that months are not counted to lower the price owed to הקדש

steps.title: The verse says years, not months
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from ויקרא 27:18, which says the כהן calculates 'according to the years that remain'. Years are counted, not months.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the כהן shall calculate the money for him according to the years that remain.' You count years, and you do not count months.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question with a פסוק. Because the תורה says 'years', only full years lower the price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes how the price drops as the יובל gets closer. It speaks only of 'years', so the ברייתא learns that leftover months cannot be used to lower the price.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (introduces a proof from a פסוק)
And he shall calculate
The years that remain (until the יובל)

steps.whatToRemember: The source for 'we don't count months against הקדש' is the word 'years' in ויקרא 27:18.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And the priest shall calculate the money for him
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:18

phrases.english: according to the years that remain" —
years you calculate,
but you do not calculate months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 with a פסוק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'years' in ויקרא 27:18 shows that only full years are counted, not months

steps.title: Asking for the source that the Temple may treat months as a year
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks a second question: where do we learn that הקדש may treat a few months as a full year if it wants to?
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that if you want to treat months as a year, you may do so?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now looks for the source of the other half of the משנה's rule: 'but הקדש does count months'. It is setting up an explanation that comes later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we learned that leftover months can't lower the price owed to הקדש. Now the question goes the other way: may the כהן, acting for הקדש, count months as a full year when that helps הקדש?

keyTerms.meaning: To treat months as a full year
Wants (here, the כהן acting for הקדש)

phrases.english: From where do we know that if you want
phrases.notes: 'You' here is the כהן, who acts for הקדש.

phrases.english: to make months into a year, you may do so?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִין שֶׁאִם אַתָּה רוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת חֳדָשִׁים לַשָּׁנָה עוֹשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the second half of the משנה's rule, the opposite side of step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק allows הקדש to treat months as a full year when that helps it

steps.title: When would this matter? A field consecrated in the middle of the 48th year
steps.stepSummary: Before giving the source, the גמרא asks when הקדש would want to count months as a year. The example is a field consecrated in the middle of the 48th year.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? For example, where he consecrated it in the middle of the 48th year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to describe a real case where counting months as a year makes a difference. It asks 'what is the case' and answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the field is consecrated halfway through the 48th year, about a year and a half is left until the יובל. Because partial years are not subtracted (step 1), that counts as two years, so the low per-year price applies. If הקדש treats the passed half-year as a full year, only one year is left. The per-year rate is not used with less than two years before the יובל, so the full price of fifty שקלים per בית כור would apply.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
That he consecrated it (the field)
In the middle, halfway through
Forty-eight (the 48th year of the יובל cycle)

steps.confusionAlert: Here counting months as a year leads to a higher price, because it pushes the case below the two-year minimum. In step 1 the price is not lowered for partial years. Both rules always work in favor of הקדש.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
For example, where he consecrated it
in the middle of the forty-eighth year.
phrases.notes: A year and a half is left, which normally rounds up to two years. If the half-year that passed counts as a full year, only one year is left.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי — כְּגוֹן דְּאַקְדְּשֵׁיהּ בְּפַלְגָא דְּאַרְבְּעִין וְתַמְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the case behind the question of step 6 before the source is given
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what situation would הקדש benefit from counting months as a year
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When the field was consecrated in the middle of the 48th year

steps.title: The source: the כהן reckons in any case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers its second question from the words 'וחשב לו הכהן'. These words mean the כהן calculates in whatever way suits הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Then the כהן shall reckon for him.' That means in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the source it asked for in Step 6. That source is the phrase 'וחשב לו הכהן'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 showed that months are not counted to lower the price owed to הקדש. Now the extra word 'וחשב' (and he shall reckon) teaches that the כהן has open freedom in his calculation. So in a case like the field consecrated in the middle of the 48th year, he may count the leftover months as a full year when that helps הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (introduces a verse as the source)
And he shall reckon/calculate
In any case; in every way

steps.whatToRemember: Months never lower the price owed to הקדש (from 'השנים הנותרות'). But הקדש may count months as a full year when that helps it (from 'וחשב לו הכהן').

phrases.english: The verse states:
"Then the priest shall reckon for him,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:18

phrases.english: in any case.
phrases.notes: He means the כהן's calculation isn't locked into one method. He can count months as a year when that helps הקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the question asked in Step 6, after Step 7 described the case where it matters.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where do we learn that הקדש may count months as a full year?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'וחשב לו הכהן': the כהן reckons in any case, so he may count months as a year in favor of הקדש.

steps.title: The basic redemption price and what is measured
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: during the time of the יובל, a consecrated field is redeemed at 50 שקלים for each area sown with a חומר of barley. Deep crevices and tall boulders (ten טפחים) are not included in the measurement.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who consecrates his field at a time when the יובל is in effect pays 50 silver שקלים for each area sown with a חומר of barley. If the field has crevices ten טפחים deep, or boulders ten טפחים high, they are not measured with the field. If they are smaller than that, they are measured with it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the fixed price for redeeming a consecrated ancestral field and tells us which parts of the land are left out of the measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The price is not based on what the field is worth. It is a fixed rate by area: 50 שקלים for an area that takes a חומר of barley seed. A crevice or boulder of ten טפחים counts as a separate area, so it is not measured. Anything smaller is treated as part of the field.

keyTerms.meaning: One who consecrates (gives to הקדש)
The Jubilee, every 50th year, when fields return to their owners
A large dry measure, the same as a כור (30 סאה)
Crevices; low hollows in the ground
Handbreadths

steps.confusionAlert: The 50 שקלים is not a price per year. It is the price for the whole 49-year cycle. The next part of the משנה divides it by the years that remain.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who consecrates his field at a time when the Jubilee is in effect,
gives, for an area sown with a homer of barley,
"fifty silver shekels."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:16

phrases.aramaic: הָיוּ שָׁם נְקָעִים עֲמוּקִּים עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
phrases.english: If there were crevices there ten handbreadths deep,
or boulders ten handbreadths high —
they are not measured with it,
less than this —
they are measured with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The redemption price is 50 shekels for an area sown with a חומר of barley. Crevices or boulders of ten טפחים are not measured with the field; smaller ones are.

steps.title: Paying by the years left, all at once
steps.stepSummary: If the field was consecrated a few years before the יובל, the owner pays a סלע and a פונדיון for each year left. He must pay the whole sum together, not year by year.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he consecrated it two or three years before the יובל, he pays a סלע and a פונדיון for each year. If he says, 'I will pay each year's amount during that year,' we do not listen to him. He must pay all of it at once.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It explains how the 50 שקלים is divided by the years left until the יובל, and it says the money must be paid in one payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 50 שקלים covers the whole cycle, each remaining year costs about a סלע plus a small coin. The owner cannot spread the payment over time like rent. Redemption is a single purchase, so he pays the full amount up front.

keyTerms.meaning: A silver coin, the same as the Torah's שקל
A small coin worth a fraction of a סלע
All of it together, in one payment

phrases.aramaic: הִקְדִּישָׁהּ שְׁתַּיִם וְשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים לִפְנֵי הַיּוֹבֵל —
phrases.english: If he consecrated it two or three years before the Jubilee —
he gives a sela and a pundeyon per year,
and if he said:
"I will give each year's amount during that year" —
we do not listen to him;
rather, he gives all of it at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִקְדִּישָׁהּ שְׁתַּיִם וְשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים לִפְנֵי הַיּוֹבֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה by dividing the 50-shekel price by the years that remain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He pays a סלע and a פונדיון for each year left until the יובל, and he must pay the whole sum at once.

steps.title: Owner and anyone else: the only difference is the חומש
steps.stepSummary: The same price applies whether the owner or anyone else redeems the field. The only difference is that the owner adds a fifth (חומש).
steps.simpleTranslation: The rule is the same for the owner and for anyone else. What is the difference between the owner and anyone else? Only that the owner adds a fifth, and anyone else does not add a fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes by comparing an owner who redeems his field with a stranger who redeems it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both pay the same fixed rate and must pay all at once. The owner alone must add an extra חומש on top of the price. Anyone else pays only the basic amount.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner (the one who consecrated the field)
An added fifth on top of the price
Any other person

steps.whatToRemember: Fixed price by area, divided by the years left, paid all at once. The owner alone adds a חומש.

phrases.english: Both the owner and any person [are the same];
what is the difference between the owner and any person?
Only that the owner gives a fifth,
and any other person does not give a fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה by saying who the payment rules apply to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner and anyone else redeem at the same rate. Only the owner adds a חומש.

steps.title: Measured by seed, sown by hand
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא defines 'זרע חומר': the area that takes a כור of seed, not the area that produces a כור of crop. The sowing is measured as done by hand, not by oxen.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: a כור of seed, not a כור of crop. Sowing by hand, not sowing by oxen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by bringing a ברייתא that explains exactly how to measure the area described in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בזרע חומר' could mean the area that grows a חומר of grain. The ברייתא says they mean the area into which a חומר of seed is sown, which is a much larger area. It also uses hand sowing as the standard rather than oxen, because the way the seed is sown changes how much land a כור covers.

keyTerms.meaning: A large measure (30 סאה), the same as a חומר
Seed that is sown
Grain crop that is harvested
Sowing; scattering of seed

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It was taught: a kor of seed,
and not a kor of crop;
sowing by hand,
and not sowing by oxen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה's phrase 'בזרע חומר שעורים' from Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The area is measured by a כור of seed, not a כור of crop, as sown by hand rather than by oxen.

steps.title: Average density of sowing
steps.stepSummary: לוי's ברייתא adds that the sowing is measured at an average density, neither thick nor thin.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי taught: not thick and not sparse, but average.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ברייתא adds one more detail to the measurement: how thickly the seed is spread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with hand sowing, one person may scatter seed thickly and another thinly, and that changes the area. לוי sets an average density as the standard, so the price does not depend on one farmer's habits.

keyTerms.meaning: Thick, dense
Thin, sparse
Average, in the middle

steps.whatToRemember: The standard area is a כור of seed, sown by hand, at an average density.

phrases.english: Levi taught:
not dense and not sparse,
but average.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי לֵוִי: לֹא מְעֻבֶּה וְלָא מֵידֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further detail to the measurement standard given in Step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sowing is measured at an average density, neither thick nor sparse.

steps.title: Why aren't the deep crevices consecrated on their own?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line in the משנה about deep crevices and asks why they are not consecrated and measured as their own area.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said that deep crevices are not measured with the field. But the crevices can be sown too, so they should be consecrated on their own!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule about deep crevices and challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A crevice ten טפחים deep is still ground that can be planted. So why leave it out? It should be הקדש like the rest of the field and be added to the price.

keyTerms.meaning: Crevices, low dips in the ground
On their own, as a separate unit
Let them become consecrated

phrases.english: If there were deep crevices there, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from Step 9: crevices ten טפחים deep are not measured.

phrases.english: But let them be consecrated on their own!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the crevices clause of the משנה from Step 9 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that deep crevices are left out of the measurement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The crevices can be sown, so they should be consecrated and included in the price.

steps.title: Even a tiny field can be consecrated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible answer: someone might say the crevices are too small to be consecrated, but a ברייתא teaches that a field of any size can be הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say that the crevices are smaller than a בית כור, so they are not consecrated. But a ברייתא teaches: Why does the פסוק say 'field'? The פסוק speaks of an area sown with a חומר of barley, so I might think only a field that big counts. How do we include a לתך, half a לתך, a סאה, a תרקב, or half a תרקב? The word 'field' teaches that any size counts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes its question stronger by knocking down an easy answer before anyone offers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The easy answer is that a crevice is too small to count. The ברייתא learns from the word 'שדה' that even a very small field is consecrated. So the size of the crevices cannot be the reason they are left out, and the question from Step 14 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (the גמרא raises a possible answer in order to reject it)
An area that takes a כור of seed to sow
Half a כור
Half a סאה
To include
In any case, of any size

phrases.english: And if you would say,
since they are not a beit kor in size,
they are not consecrated,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: but isn't it taught in a baraita:
"Field": why does the verse need to say it?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:16

phrases.english: Since it is stated
"the sowing of a ḥomer of barley at fifty shekels of silver,"

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁהִקְדִּישׁ כָּעִנְיָן הַזֶּה,

steps.title: The crevices are full of water
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא בר חמא answers that the משנה means crevices filled with water, which cannot be sown.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר עוקבא בר חמא said: Here the משנה means crevices full of water, which cannot be sown.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The price of a consecrated field depends on how much of it can be sown. Crevices full of water cannot be sown at all, so they are not part of the measured area. Their size is not the issue.

steps.title: Years in הקדש Are Also Subtracted From the Price
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'ונגרע מערכך' that the years the field sat in הקדש are also subtracted. The redeemer pays a סלע and a פונדיון only for each year left until יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said that if he consecrated the field two or three years before יובל, he pays per year. The רבנן taught: 'And a deduction shall be made from your valuation' means that even the years while the field was in הקדש are subtracted. So whether הקדש ate the field's produce for a year or two, or did not eat it and the field just sat there, he pays a סלע and a פונדיון for each year that is left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that explains which years get subtracted from the redemption price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think only the years before he consecrated the field get subtracted. The ברייתא says the years the field sat in הקדש are subtracted too. It makes no difference whether הקדש actually used the produce or not.

steps.title: 'The Money' Means One Full Payment
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'וחשב לו הכהן את הכסף' teaches that the money must be paid all together. This rule applies to the owner and to anyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Then the כהן shall reckon for him the money.' This means the money must be paid all together, as one sum. This is true both for the owner and for anyone else who redeems the field.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with a פסוק and says the rule applies to every redeemer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The money' is read as one complete sum, not small pieces spread over the years. The ברייתא then adds that the owner and an outsider follow the same rule here.

steps.title: The Owner Adds a Fifth, Others Do Not
steps.stepSummary: If the owner and an outsider are the same here, what is different between them? Only the owner adds a חומש.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is the difference between the owner and anyone else? The owner pays an extra fifth, and anyone else does not pay the extra fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks what does make the owner different from an outsider, and answers right away: the חומש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both must pay in one lump sum, one might think they are the same in every way. The ברייתא points out the one difference: only an owner who redeems his own consecrated field adds a חומש.

steps.title: New משנה: Who Keeps a Redeemed Field at יובל
steps.stepSummary: If the owner redeems the field, he keeps it at יובל. If his son redeems it, it goes back to the father. If an outsider or another relative redeems it and the owner then buys it from him, it goes to the כהנים at יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a man consecrated his field and then redeemed it, it does not leave his hands at יובל. If his son redeemed it, at יובל it goes back to the father. If someone else or one of the other relatives redeemed it, and then the owner redeemed it from that person, at יובל it goes to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets out three cases of who redeemed a consecrated field and what happens to the field at יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the owner himself redeems the field, it stays his for good. A son's redemption counts as the family's, so the field returns to the father. But if an outsider or another relative redeemed it first, buying it back from them does not save it, and it goes to the כהנים at יובל.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of a new משנה

From his hand: from his possession

steps.confusionAlert: In the last case the owner does end up redeeming the field, but from the other person, not from הקדש. That is why it still goes to the כהנים.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Redemption by the owner or his son keeps the field in the family at יובל. If an outsider or another relative redeemed it first, it goes to the כהנים at יובל even if the owner later buys it back.
steps.whatToRemember: What matters is who redeemed the field from הקדש: the owner or his son keeps it in the family, while anyone else's redemption sends it to the כהנים at יובל.

steps.title: A priest who redeemed the field must share it with all the priests
steps.stepSummary: If a כהן redeemed the field and holds it at יובל, he cannot keep it. It is divided among all the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of the כהנים redeemed the field and it is in his hands when יובל comes, he may not say: 'Since it goes to the כהנים at יובל, and it is already in my hands, it is mine.' Instead, it leaves his hands and is divided among all his fellow כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more case to the list of who ends up with the field at יובל. Here the person who redeemed the field is himself a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know a field like this goes to the כהנים at יובל. A כהן holding it might think he can just keep it, since he is a כהן and it is already his. The משנה says no: it belongs to all the כהנים as a group, so it leaves his hands and is split among all of them.

steps.whatToRemember: A field that goes to the כהנים at יובל belongs to all the כהנים together. Even a כהן who redeemed it and holds it cannot keep it for himself.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that because the holder is a כהן, the field has already 'arrived' at the כהנים. The field is given to the כהנים as a group, not to whichever כהן happens to hold it.
